name: Asylum and Refugee Status (N/B/F Permits)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires SEM recognition as a refugee under the Asylum Act — grants a full B permit with genuine residence and eventual settlement prospects.

requirement_groups.name: Provisional admission (F permit — de facto long-lasting)

requirements.blocker_text: This applies to those not granted refugee status but who cannot be lawfully, safely, or reasonably returned — issued for 12 months, renewed annually by the canton. Despite the name 'provisional,' this status is frequently held long-term: at end-2024, 35,239 people held F status, of whom 15,409 (44%) had held it for more than 7 years.

evidence_required.document: Evidence supporting the persecution or non-removability claim

outcome.duration_length: B permit (recognised refugee): tracks the standard permit cycle. F permit: 12 months, renewed annually — genuinely long-lasting in practice

sources.title: Provisional admission (F permit) - State Secretariat for Migration

notes: GENUINE, WELL-DOCUMENTED 'PROVISIONAL IN NAME ONLY' FINDING — one of the most striking statistics in this entire multi-country dataset: at end-2024, 35,239 people held F (provisional admission) status, and 15,409 of them (44%) had held it for MORE THAN 7 YEARS — meaning the modal experience of 'provisional' admission in Switzerland is genuinely long-term, not provisional in any meaningful sense. This is captured via a group-level outcome_override on the F-permit group, since its actual real-world trajectory (leads_to_pr eventually, after years of annual renewal) differs materially from what the bare word 'provisional' would suggest. Switzerland participates in the Dublin/AMMR system DESPITE NOT BEING AN EU MEMBER — a genuinely distinctive bilateral arrangement, issuing 9,947 take-charge/take-back requests in 2024 (12,933 in 2023), a real and substantial volume worth noting. N permit (asylum seeker during the procedure) is not separately modeled as its own group here since it carries no independent outcome of its own — it resolves into either the recognised-refugee or provisional-admission group, or removal.
